title: What is the area of this quadrilateral?
description: A quadrilateral has a diagonal of twenty two centimetres, and the heights from the two opposite corners to it are both three centimetres. The diagonal splits the shape into two triangles, and their areas add up to sixty six square centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: a diagonal splits a quadrilateral into two triangles, so its area is the sum of two triangle areas. Watch for students who forget the half.

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 1)
video_script.why: The child applies the two triangles on a diagonal method of the solved example to a new quadrilateral.
video_script.substitution: Use the diagonal AC as the common base, find each triangle from its height, and add the two areas.
video_script.anchor: the book's quadrilateral ABCD with the diagonal AC = 22 cm and the perpendiculars BM = 3 cm and DN = 3 cm to AC
video_script.payoff_line: The area is sixty six square centimetres
never_show: the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: the diagonal AC splits ABCD into ΔABC and ΔACD with the common base AC = 22 cm
video_script.design: One quadrilateral all video. The diagonal makes two triangles with the same base and their areas are added.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='quad'/>Here is a quadrilateral eigh B C D. Its diagonal eigh C is twenty two centimetres.
<bookmark mark='bm'/>The height B M from B down to eigh C is three centimetres.
<bookmark mark='dn'/>The height D N from D down to eigh C is also three centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the area of the quadrilateral?

beats.on_screen: the shape holds still and the whole quadrilateral glows with its question mark

marks.stop: the whole quadrilateral glows in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the diagonal AC lights up and splits the quadrilateral into two triangles; the rule area = 1/2 × base × height

marks.diag: the diagonal eigh C lights up
marks.two: the quadrilateral splits into the triangles eigh B C and eigh C D
marks.area: the rule area = 1/2 × base × height is written

narration: <bookmark mark='diag'/>Use the same method as before. A diagonal splits a four sided shape into two triangles.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Here the diagonal eigh C is the base of both triangles.
<bookmark mark='area'/>Each area is half of base times height.

beats.on_screen: Given: AC = 22 cm; BM ⊥ AC, BM = 3 cm; DN ⊥ AC, DN = 3 cm

marks.given: the diagonal and the two heights are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the diagonal eigh C is twenty two centimetres.
The heights B M and D N to eigh C are three centimetres each.

beats.on_screen: To find: the area of ABCD

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the quadrilateral eigh B C D.

marks.tri: triangle eigh B C is outlined with the base eigh C and the height B M

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step one, take the triangle eigh B C. Its base is eigh C and its height is B M.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of twenty two times three is thirty three square centimetres.

marks.tri: triangle eigh C D is outlined with the base eigh C and the height D N

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, take the triangle eigh C D. It has the same base eigh C, and its height is D N.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of twenty two times three is also thirty three square centimetres.

marks.join: the two triangles slide together to make the quadrilateral

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step three, the two triangles together make the whole quadrilateral.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add thirty three and thirty three to get sixty six.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, check it another way.
Both triangles share the base eigh C, so add the heights, three plus three, which is six.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Half of twenty two times six is sixty six.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The area is sixty six square centimetres.
